itineraries.title: Food Truck Friday & Karaoke Under the Stars — Durham
itineraries.theme: A nearly-free Durham Friday: farm stand, BBQ off a truck, then outdoor karaoke — with downtown improv as the thunderstorm backup
itineraries.drive_time: ~25 min Raleigh → RTP. North Durham market to Glass Jug RTP is about 20 min; RTP to downtown Durham (Mettlesome) about 15 min.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$35 (market and karaoke are free; spend is the food truck plus an optional $9 comedy ticket)
itineraries.overview: Friday tops out near 79°F with scattered storms, so this one is built to pivot. Start at the North Durham Friday market, roll into Food Truck Friday at Glass Jug in RTP for Smoking Aces BBQ, then stay for free Karaoke Under the Stars on the patio. If the radar lights up, downtown Durham's Mettlesome has back-to-back indoor comedy for under $10.

afternoon.title: North Durham Friday Evening Farmers' Market
afternoon.notes: Small, easygoing afternoon market — good for peaches and a snack before dinner. Outdoor, so check the sky first.

evening.title: Food Truck Friday: Smoking Aces BBQ at Glass Jug RTP
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab - RTP, 5410 NC-55 Suite V, Durham, NC 27713
evening.notes: No cover — you only pay for what you eat and drink. Covered patio seating means a passing storm doesn't end the night.

evening.title: Karaoke Under the Stars at Glass Jug RTP
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab - RTP, 5410 NC-55 Suite V, Durham, NC 27713
evening.notes: Free outdoor karaoke — stay put after the food truck and you've spent nothing on entertainment all night.

evening.title: America $2.50 — A Mettlesome Sketch Comedy Show
evening.notes: Storm plan: trade the patio for downtown Durham sketch comedy indoors.

evening.title: Hush Hush
evening.notes: Late indoor add-on at Mettlesome if you went the comedy route — $9 and you're out by 10.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan glazed cake donut plus a side of home fries
food.notes: Durham breakfast-and-lunch staple with a reliable vegan donut case. Kitchen winds down mid-afternoon — go before the market.

food.place: Smoking Aces BBQ truck at Glass Jug RTP
food.vegan_dish: unknown — a BBQ truck rarely runs a vegan plate; check the board on arrival
food.vegetarian_dish: Sides plate (slaw, beans, mac) if offered
food.notes: This is dinner if you stay for karaoke. Plant-based eaters should eat beforehand — see Vegan Flava Cafe below.

food.vegan_dish: Plant-based soul-food plate — jerk-spiced tofu with collards and mac
food.vegetarian_dish: Everything on the menu (the kitchen is fully plant-based)
food.notes: Fully vegan Durham kitchen and the safest plant-based dinner on this route. Hours are limited — confirm before driving over.

alternatives.leg: Karaoke Under the Stars (outdoor patio, 8:00 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Stay on the Glass Jug RTP patio for free outdoor karaoke.
alternatives.rain: Drive 15 min to Mettlesome in downtown Durham for indoor sketch comedy at 7:30 PM and Hush Hush at 9:00 PM ($9).

alternatives.leg: North Durham Friday Evening Farmers' Market (outdoor, 3:00 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk the stalls and pick up produce for the weekend.
alternatives.rain: Skip it and go straight to Glass Jug RTP — the taproom opens well before the 5:00 PM truck.

practical_notes: Glass Jug RTP is at 5410 NC-55 Suite V, Durham — free surface parking right at the door.
Both Glass Jug events are free to attend; budget only for food and beer.
Mettlesome is in downtown Durham — use the Durham Centre or Corcoran Street decks; street parking is free after 7 PM.
Storm timing Friday is scattered rather than all-day; a 30-minute wait usually clears it.
Restaurant menus and hours change — confirm the vegan options by phone before you commit the drive.

itineraries.title: Market Morning, Museum Afternoon, Rock Club Night — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A full classic Raleigh Saturday that stays free until dinner
itineraries.drive_time: All inside Raleigh: North Hills → downtown ~12 min, downtown → NCMA ~12 min, NCMA → Pour House ~12 min.

weather.summary: Chance Rain Showers then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$60 (markets, Capitol tour and NCMA galleries are free; spend is the trolley, dinner and a $15 show)
itineraries.overview: Saturday is a comfortable 81°F with only a chance of showers, which makes this the week's best all-day Raleigh loop. Do the Midtown market early, add the flea market at the fairgrounds if you want to dig, take a free guided tour of the State Capitol, spend the hot part of the afternoon inside the NC Museum of Art, then finish at the Pour House for a $15 show.

morning.title: Midtown Farmers' Market
morning.location: The Commons at North Hills, Raleigh
morning.notes: Get there early — the good produce and the shade both go first.

morning.title: The Raleigh Market (Saturday)
morning.notes: Optional swap for the farmers' market: a big indoor/outdoor flea at the fairgrounds. Free admission, paid parking.

morning.title: North Carolina State Capitol Guided Tour
morning.notes: Free guided tour of the 1840 Capitol, and it's air-conditioned — a good hedge as the day heats up.

afternoon.title: Historic Raleigh Trolley Tour
afternoon.price: $10 adults, $6 youth (7-17), free ages 6 and under
afternoon.notes: Alternative to the Capitol tour: a narrated trolley loop of historic Raleigh departing from Mordecai. $10 and worth it with kids in tow.

afternoon.title: Public Tour at the NC Museum of Art
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh, NC 27607
afternoon.notes: Docent-led tour of the collection. The People's Collection galleries are free to enter.

afternoon.title: Art on the Dot
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh, NC 27607
afternoon.notes: Short drop-in art activity right after the tour — easy to stack the two.

evening.title: Keith Allen w/ Royal Jelly
evening.location: The Pour House Music Hall, Raleigh
evening.notes: $15 downtown rock show. Doors are well before the 9:00 PM start — grab dinner on Blount Street first.

food.vegan_dish: Oatmeal with fruit and a nut-milk latte
food.notes: Quick pre-market coffee stop; there's a location near North Hills.

food.vegan_dish: Grain bowl with tofu, greens and tahini
food.notes: Fast, cold and plant-forward — the right call before an afternoon indoors.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan Southern fried 'chicken' and waffles
food.notes: Entirely vegetarian/vegan kitchen downtown, a short walk from the Pour House. Reservations strongly recommended on a Saturday.

alternatives.good_weather: Walk the North Hills commons market in the cool part of the morning.
alternatives.rain: Head to The Raleigh Market at the fairgrounds instead — much of it is under roof.

alternatives.good_weather: Take the open trolley loop from Mordecai.
alternatives.rain: Do the free indoor State Capitol guided tour at the same hour instead.

practical_notes: NCMA parking is free and the People's Collection galleries cost nothing — an easy way to keep this day cheap.
The Raleigh Market charges for parking at the fairgrounds even though admission is free.
Downtown Raleigh street parking is free on Saturdays; the Blount Street deck is closest to the Pour House.
Budget about 12 minutes between each leg — nothing on this route is more than a short hop.
Saturday's rain chance is highest early and late; the midday museum block is the natural place to wait out a shower.
Confirm restaurant hours and menu items before you go — they change seasonally.

itineraries.title: Get Messy, Get Outside, Get to the Show — Durham Family Saturday
itineraries.theme: A kid-built Durham Saturday: a ranger hike, a museum messtival, and a youth musical matinee
itineraries.drive_time: ~30 min Raleigh → Durham. Sandy Creek Park → Museum of Life and Science is about 12 min; museum → Murphey School Auditorium about 10 min.

weather.summary: Chance Rain Showers then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$80 for a family of four (hike free; museum admission is the main cost, plus matinee tickets)
itineraries.overview: Everything here is aimed at kids and it all sits within ten minutes of itself in Durham. Burn off the morning on a family hike at Sandy Creek, then hand the day over to the Museum of Life and Science, where 'Let's Get Messy!' is exactly what it sounds like. A 2:00 PM youth production of Newsies Jr. closes it out indoors — which is also your rain plan.

morning.title: Family Fun Hike at Sandy Creek Park
morning.notes: Easy guided family hike first thing, before the heat and the storm chance build.

morning.title: Let's Get Messy! (Messtival)
morning.location: Museum of Life and Science, Durham
morning.notes: Hands-on mess-making included with museum admission. Bring a full change of clothes — this is not a figure of speech.

afternoon.title: From Here On: Shaping Our Future
afternoon.location: Museum of Life and Science, Durham
afternoon.notes: Stay in the museum after lunch — this exhibit is part of the same admission, indoor and cool.

afternoon.title: STC Presents: Newsies Jr.
afternoon.notes: Youth-cast matinee of Newsies Jr. — about 90 minutes and a good length for younger kids.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan cake donut and a fruit cup
food.notes: Grab-and-go before the 9:00 AM hike; there's usually a line on Saturdays.

food.place: Museum of Life and Science cafe
food.vegan_dish: unknown — cafe menu varies; pack a plant-based lunch to be safe
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese pizza or grilled cheese, typically available
food.notes: The museum has picnic areas for outside food, which is cheaper and more reliable for allergy or vegan needs.

food.vegan_dish: Seasonal vegetable plate with bread from the bakery
food.notes: German-leaning Durham bakery-cafe with a shaded patio; kid-tolerant and open after the matinee.

alternatives.leg: Family Fun Hike at Sandy Creek Park (outdoor, 9:00 AM)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the guided hike — shaded creekside trail, good for small legs.
alternatives.rain: Skip to the Museum of Life and Science at opening, or duck into the Nasher Museum at Duke, which is free.

alternatives.leg: Museum of Life and Science outdoor areas (Dinosaur Trail, Butterfly House)
alternatives.good_weather: Work the outdoor trail and farmyard between indoor exhibits.
alternatives.rain: The messtival and 'From Here On' are both indoors — you can spend the whole visit under roof.

practical_notes: Museum of Life and Science admission is the single biggest cost here; members get in free and it pays for itself in two visits.
Bring a full change of clothes and a towel for the messtival — plan on the kids getting genuinely covered.
Sandy Creek Park has a small gravel lot that fills on Saturday mornings; arrive a few minutes early.
Murphey School Auditorium is a school venue — parking is on-site and free.
The Nasher Museum at Duke is free and 10 minutes away if you need an unplanned indoor hour.
Confirm restaurant hours before you go — Durham kitchens vary on weekends.

itineraries.title: Carrboro Market, Free Galleries, Big Broadway — Chapel Hill & Carrboro
itineraries.theme: The cheapest cultured day of the week: a 7 AM market, two free museums, and a $10 musical
itineraries.drive_time: ~35 min Raleigh → Chapel Hill. Carrboro Town Commons → Ackland is about 6 min; Ackland → Gillings Center about 5 min. Most of the day is walkable once parked.

weather.summary: Chance Rain Showers then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $10–$45 (market browsing and both Ackland exhibitions are free; the musical is $10–$20)
itineraries.overview: This is the week's best value. The Carrboro Farmers' Market opens at 7:00 AM, the Ackland Art Museum is free and has two new acquisition shows up, and PlayMakers' Hello, Dolly! runs $10–$20 at the Gillings Center that evening. Park once near Franklin Street and you can walk most of it.

morning.title: Carrboro Farmers' Market (Saturday)
morning.notes: One of the strongest producer-only markets in the state, and it opens at 7:00 AM — go early and beat both the heat and the crowd.

morning.title: Care and Concern: Recent Acquisitions of Modern and Contemporary Art
morning.notes: Free admission at the Ackland. Pair it with the African art show in the next gallery.

morning.title: Continental Shift: Recent Acquisitions of African Art
morning.notes: Same building, same free admission — an easy second exhibition.

evening.title: Hello, Dolly!
evening.location: Joan H. Gillings Center for Dramatic Art, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: PlayMakers' summer production at $10–$20 — remarkable value for a full staged musical.

evening.title: maryjo w/ Brooke Alexx
evening.notes: Alternative evening: an indie bill at Local 506 on Franklin Street if a musical isn't your thing.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan pastry and coffee from the bakery counter
food.vegetarian_dish: Breakfast burrito from the hot bar
food.notes: Directly beside the Town Commons — you can eat on the lawn without moving the car.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel plate with hummus, tabbouleh and stuffed grape leaves
food.notes: A very large vegan-friendly mezze bar on Franklin Street; easy to build a fully plant-based plate.

food.vegan_dish: Chana masala with rice
food.notes: Long-running Franklin Street kitchen with clearly marked vegan dishes, five minutes from the theater.

alternatives.good_weather: Walk the full market at the Town Commons.
alternatives.rain: Duck into Weaver Street Market next door and go to the Ackland when it opens at 10:00 AM.

alternatives.good_weather: Hello, Dolly! at the Gillings Center ($10–$20).
alternatives.rain: Both options are indoors — no change needed. Local 506 is the smaller, later alternative.

practical_notes: Carrboro Town Commons has a free lot but it fills by about 8:30 AM on Saturdays.
The Ackland Art Museum is free — no ticket needed for either exhibition.
Park once in the Franklin Street decks and walk the Ackland, lunch and dinner legs.
Hello, Dolly! at $10–$20 is the single best entertainment value in the store this week — buy ahead, summer runs sell out.
Confirm restaurant hours and menu items before you go; Franklin Street hours shift in the summer.

itineraries.title: Bubbles, Soul Food and a Cabaret — Downtown Raleigh Sunday
itineraries.theme: Two free outdoor festivals back-to-back downtown, then an intimate evening cabaret
itineraries.drive_time: Moore Square to City Plaza is a 5-minute walk; the fairgrounds are about 12 min by car. Park once downtown for the afternoon.

weather.summary: Chance Rain Showers then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$50 (Bubble Festival and Taste of Soul are free to attend; spend is food and an evening ticket)
itineraries.overview: Sunday runs warmer at 86°F, but the two marquee events are free, outdoors and a five-minute walk apart downtown. The Bubble Festival takes over Moore Square at 11:00 AM; the Taste of Soul NC finale lands at City Plaza at 1:00 PM. Cool off at the NC Museum of Art in the late afternoon, then finish with Theatre Raleigh's cabaret.

morning.title: The Raleigh Market (Sunday)
morning.notes: Optional early stop — free admission flea market at the fairgrounds before the downtown festivals open.

morning.title: The Bubble Festival (2nd Annual)
morning.notes: Outdoor festival in Moore Square — shade is limited, so bring water and hats for kids.

afternoon.title: Taste of Soul NC Series Finale (Raleigh Edition)
afternoon.notes: Free to attend, five minutes on foot from Moore Square. Food is pay-as-you-go from the vendors.

afternoon.title: Art on the Dot
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh, NC 27607
afternoon.notes: Air-conditioned reset after four hours outside in the high 80s.

evening.title: TR Sings... Songs You're Too Old to Sing, but Why Not
evening.notes: Small-room cabaret to close the weekend — an easy, seated, indoor finish.

food.vegan_dish: Sourdough loaf and a fruit hand pie
food.notes: Stone-milled bakery south of downtown; go early, they sell out.

food.place: Taste of Soul NC vendors at City Plaza
food.vegan_dish: unknown — varies by vendor; ask each booth directly
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — mac and cheese and candied yams are common at soul-food booths
food.notes: Lunch is the festival itself. Vendor lineups aren't published in advance, so plant-based eaters should have a backup.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan mezze plate — falafel, hummus, tabbouleh and grape leaves
food.vegetarian_dish: Spinach pie with a Greek salad
food.notes: Lebanese counter-service with a clearly labeled vegan case; quick enough to fit before a 7:00 PM curtain.

alternatives.leg: The Bubble Festival at Moore Square (outdoor, 11:00 AM)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the full festival in the square.
alternatives.rain: Shift to the NC Museum of Art early — the 1:00 PM public tour and 2:30 PM Art on the Dot are both indoors.

alternatives.leg: Taste of Soul NC at City Plaza (outdoor, 1:00 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Eat your way through the plaza in the open air.
alternatives.rain: Grab food from the covered edges of the plaza, or fall back to Sassool indoors.

practical_notes: Downtown Raleigh street parking is free on Sundays — park once between Moore Square and City Plaza and walk both festivals.
86°F with limited shade at Moore Square: bring water, and plan the museum block as your cooling hour.
The NCMA public tour at 1:00 PM is an indoor alternative if the festivals get rained out.
Vendor-based food events rarely publish vegan options ahead of time — Sassool is the reliable plant-based fallback.
Confirm restaurant hours before you go; several downtown kitchens close early on Sundays.

itineraries.title: Bob Dylan at Red Hat, Then Late Night on Martin Street — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: The week's marquee concert, with a free late show to stretch the night
itineraries.drive_time: Red Hat Amphitheater and Kings are both in downtown Raleigh — about a 10-minute walk apart.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $40–$150 (Dylan tickets are the cost; the late show at Kings is free)
itineraries.overview: Tuesday is the hottest day of the window at 92°F, and it holds the week's biggest show: Bob Dylan with Lucinda Williams and Jimmie Vaughan at Red Hat Amphitheater. Eat somewhere air-conditioned first, take the 6:30 PM downbeat outdoors as the sun drops, then walk to Kings for a free 18+ late show. Durham Bulls baseball is the alternative if Dylan is sold out.

evening.title: Bob Dylan w/ Lucinda Williams and Jimmie Vaughan & The Tilt-A-Whirl Band
evening.notes: Outdoor amphitheater on a 92°F day — the bowl stays hot until sundown. Hydrate before you go in.

evening.title: Open Decks - DJ Networking + Dancing
evening.notes: No-cover basement bar a short walk from Red Hat if you want air conditioning and a DJ.

evening.title: Sub Rosa (Late Show)
evening.notes: Free 18+ late show at Kings — the cheapest way to keep the night going after the amphitheater empties.

food.vegan_dish: Black bean and sweet plantain arepa with avocado sauce
food.notes: Fast Venezuelan counter service — light enough for a 92°F afternoon.

food.vegan_dish: Vegetable curry with rice (ask for it prepared without fish sauce)
food.notes: Laotian restaurant two blocks from Red Hat Amphitheater. Book ahead on a show night, and confirm the vegan preparation with your server.

alternatives.leg: Bob Dylan at Red Hat Amphitheater (outdoor, 6:30 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Take the lawn or bowl seats as the sun sets — the amphitheater is fully open-air.
alternatives.rain: Scattered evening storms are possible; the venue holds shows through light rain, but Durham Bulls baseball or the indoor Kings show are the backups.

alternatives.good_weather: Walk to Kings for the free 10:00 PM Sub Rosa late show.
alternatives.rain: Neptunes Parlour at 9:00 PM is indoors, downstairs and has no cover.

practical_notes: 92°F and mostly sunny — the Red Hat bowl radiates heat well past 7:00 PM. Bring a water bottle; the venue has refill stations.
Red Hat Amphitheater sits beside the convention center decks, the easiest downtown parking on a show night.
Kings and Neptunes share a building on Martin Street, about a 10-minute walk from Red Hat.
Sub Rosa at Kings is free and 18+; Open Decks at Neptunes has no cover.
If Dylan is sold out, Durham Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers starts at 6:45 PM the same night, about 30 minutes away.
Confirm restaurant hours and vegan preparations before you go.

itineraries.title: Market, Ballgame and a Full Moon Hike — Durham Wednesday
itineraries.theme: A midweek Durham evening built around Bulls baseball, with a moonlit trail as the wild card
itineraries.drive_time: ~30 min Raleigh → Durham. Durham Central Park → Durham Bulls Athletic Park is about 5 min on foot; the ballpark → Eno River EEC is about 20 min by car.

weather.summary: Chance Rain Showers then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$45 (market free; Bulls tickets plus food are the spend)
itineraries.overview: Start at the Wednesday edition of the Durham Farmers' Market at Durham Central Park, walk five minutes to the ballpark, and take in Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers at 6:45 PM. Rain is genuinely possible Wednesday, so keep Ponysaurus music bingo and Hi-Wire trivia in your pocket — both are free, indoors and minutes away.

afternoon.title: Durham Farmers' Market (Wednesday)
afternoon.notes: The midweek market under the Central Park pavilion — covered, so a shower doesn't cancel it.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham, NC 27701
evening.notes: Triple-A baseball five minutes' walk from the market. Outdoor — check the forecast before you leave.

evening.title: Music Bingo at Ponysaurus
evening.notes: Free rain plan a few minutes from the ballpark, and a good landing spot if the game goes to a delay.

evening.title: Full Moon Hike at the Eno River Environmental Education Center
evening.location: Eno River Environmental Education Park, Durham
evening.notes: Alternative to baseball entirely: a guided full-moon hike. It starts at 9:00 PM, so it does not stack with a 6:45 PM ballgame.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan donut and a grain bowl
food.notes: Close to Durham Central Park; a light lunch before the market.

food.vegan_dish: Plant-based soul-food plate with collards and mac
food.vegetarian_dish: Everything on the menu (fully plant-based kitchen)
food.notes: Fully vegan Durham kitchen — the dependable pre-game dinner. Hours are limited; confirm before driving over.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — availability varies by stand; a plain soft pretzel is the usual fallback
food.notes: Ballpark food is the easy option but weak on plant-based choices — eat at Vegan Flava Cafe first if that matters.

alternatives.leg: Durham Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers (outdoor, 6:45 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Take the ballgame — Triple-A baseball on a warm summer night.
alternatives.rain: Wednesday carries a real storm chance. Fall back to free indoor Music Bingo at Ponysaurus (7:00 PM) or Hammered Trivia at Hi-Wire Durham (7:00 PM).

alternatives.leg: Full Moon Hike at the Eno River (outdoor, 9:00 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Swap baseball for the guided moonlit hike — clear skies make it worthwhile.
alternatives.rain: Cancel the hike; the trail is unlit and slick when wet. Trivia at Hi-Wire is the indoor substitute.

practical_notes: The Durham Farmers' Market pavilion is covered, so the 3:00 PM leg survives a shower.
Durham Central Park to Durham Bulls Athletic Park is a five-minute walk — park once downtown.
The ballgame and the Eno River full moon hike overlap in the evening; pick one, they don't stack.
Both rain alternatives (Ponysaurus music bingo, Hi-Wire trivia) are free — a washed-out night costs nothing.
Ballpark concessions are thin on vegan options; eat beforehand if that matters.
Confirm restaurant hours before you go.

itineraries.title: Trivia First, Guitars After — Raleigh Thursday
itineraries.theme: Free bar trivia into a pick-your-price rock show, all inside downtown Raleigh
itineraries.drive_time: Vault Craft Beer, Compass Rose, Lincoln Theatre and the Pour House are all in or near downtown Raleigh — 5 to 12 minutes apart by car.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$45 (all the trivia is free; the show is $18–$41 depending which you pick)
itineraries.overview: The last night of the window is a cheap one. Every trivia night on this route is free, so the only real decision is which show to end on: Quinn Sullivan's blues guitar at the Pour House for about $18, Mammoth's tour stop at Lincoln Theatre for $41, or Derrick Stroup's stand-up at Goodnights. Note that this date sits past the National Weather Service's seven-day forecast, so no verified outlook is attached.

morning.title: Family Storytime @ Dix Park
morning.location: House of Many Porches at Dix Park, Raleigh
morning.notes: Optional free morning leg if you have kids — outdoor storytime at Dix Park.

evening.title: Hammered Trivia at Vault Craft Beer
evening.notes: Earliest start of the night's trivia — free to play, and it wraps in time for an 8:00 PM show.

evening.title: Not Rocket Science Trivia at Compass Rose Brewery
evening.notes: Alternative trivia room. Listings disagree on the start time here — one source says 7:00 PM, another 9:30 PM. Confirm with the brewery before you drive over.

evening.title: Quinn Sullivan w/ Daniel Andeson & The Heroic Dose
evening.location: The Pour House Music Hall, Raleigh
evening.notes: The value pick of the night — blues guitar at the Pour House for under $20.

evening.title: Mammoth - The End Tour
evening.notes: The bigger room and the bigger ticket, two blocks away at Lincoln Theatre.

evening.title: Derrick Stroup
evening.notes: Stand-up alternative if you'd rather laugh than stand at a rail.

food.vegan_dish: Tofu grain bowl with tahini
food.notes: Light midday option downtown.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan Southern fried 'chicken' and waffles
food.notes: All-vegetarian kitchen within walking distance of both the Pour House and Lincoln Theatre. Book ahead.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel and hummus plate
food.notes: Faster and cheaper than a sit-down dinner if trivia runs long.

alternatives.good_weather: Outdoor storytime on the Dix Park lawn.
alternatives.rain: Cancel this leg — it's fully outdoors and there's no covered substitute at the same hour.

alternatives.good_weather: Either show works; both venues are indoors.
alternatives.rain: No change — Pour House, Lincoln Theatre and Goodnights are all indoor rooms.

practical_notes: July 30 falls outside the National Weather Service's seven-day forecast window, so no verified weather is attached — check the forecast the day before.
Every trivia night on this route is free to play; the only unavoidable cost is food and a show ticket.
Compass Rose trivia has conflicting start times across sources (7:00 PM vs 9:30 PM) — call ahead.
The Pour House and Lincoln Theatre are two blocks apart, so you can decide late which show to buy.
Downtown Raleigh street parking is free after 5:00 PM on weeknights.
Confirm restaurant hours before you go.
